text: Ask a computer for zero point one plus zero point two.
It says zero point three, then fifteen zeros, then a four.
And in binary, zero point one is like one third in decimal:
Zero point zero zero zero one one zero zero one one, forever.
The computer has to round it off after fifty-two bits,
so it stores a number very slightly off.
That's why programmers don't compare decimals with equals,
and why money is usually stored as whole cents.
What does your calculator say for zero point one plus zero point two?
